messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT - High error rate and GPU NCCL timeouts observed on runtime cluster prod-us-west-2. Automatic page to @oncall and @eng-runtime. Root cause suspected: kv-cache shard pressure + continuous batching surge. Top symptoms: 5xxs on generate endpoints, GPU OOM/NCCL stalls.

oncall-bot: summary metrics: api_5xx_rate +420% over baseline, avg latency +3x for some customers, kv_cache_evictions sky-rocketing. Paged at 12:42 UTC.

alex: I can take first responder. Looking at logs now. Which model is hot?

sara: seeing sustained continuous-batching queue depth spike for model rwd-llama-13b-quant @prod. batch_size_auto jumped from 8->64 because of traffic pattern change. KV cache entries per shard exploded (~1.2M entries on shard 17).

meera: also seeing NCCL timeouts around the same time. snippet from worker logs: ```
NCCL INFO 2026-03-15 12:45:12 rank 3 : allreduce failed: timeout, rc=0x5
kv_shard=17 size=128MB partial_cache_entries=1200000
queue_depth=2456
```

jamal: That shard #17 is much bigger than others. Looks like tensor-parallel partitioning returned uneven sizes after the recent kernel change. Probably a tensor-split hashing regression. I think the continuous batching config amplified it (large batches pin many KV entries on one TP rank).

alex: initial mitigation proposal: 1) disable continuous batching globally for the model or lower max_tokens_per_batch 2) temporarily fall back to per-request routing to avoid TP-allreduce across too many ranks 3) notify SRE to restart the few stuck workers once traffic drops. Thoughts?

sara: +1. I'm pushing a feature-flag flip to reduce batch_max_tokens to 16 for model rwd-llama-13b-quant. Command: `rwctl feature-flag set runtime.continuous_batching.max_tokens=16 --env=prod --target=model:rwd-llama-13b-quant`

deploy-bot: rollout started: runtime FF change id ff_3921 -> target 100 nodes (40% initial canary).

ops_lead: notify customer_success to triage enterprise customers who reported errors. Also prepare for a full worker recycle if NCCL doesn't recover after batching reduction.

customer_success: flagged two enterprise customers (acme-inc, finco) with increased latencies and some 500s. Reached out with initial note: "we're investigating, temporary mitigations in progress, status updates every 30m". They want ETA on full fix.

meera: after reducing batch_max_tokens, we see queue depth fall ~70% in 4 minutes, 5xxs drop. However one node still reporting high partial_cache_entries and repeated NCCL retries.

jamal: that suggests uneven shard assignment persists. Need a runtime hotfix to rebalance KV cache partitioning algorithm. Quick patch: change partition from naive round-robin to consistent-hash partitioning to avoid pathological splits when tensor split boundaries shift. Proposed patch diff: ```
- shards = evenly_divide(tensors, tp_size)
+ shards = consistent_hash_partition(tensors, tp_size)
```
This avoids single-shard hotspots when a tensor boundary aligns with a large KV table.

alex: can eng-runtime build an emergency release for the runtime that updates hashing? We may be able to roll it to a subset of nodes handling that model.

eng-ml: I can validate the partition logic. If we roll a binary that changes partitioning, we'll need to ensure rolling upgrade doesn't cause KV mismatch across workers. We should implement a handshake where new workers advertise partition_version, and older workers fallback to safe single-GPU execution for that model until all ranks are compatible.

ops_lead: agree on handshake approach. Short term, do we have a safe non-invasive change? e.g., a hotpatch that forces the model to single-GPU execution (no TP) for new requests to that model while we roll? That would avoid allreduce/NCCL traffic.

sara: we can add a routing override: `rwctl route set model:rwd-llama-13b-quant --exec-mode=single-gpu --env=prod --reason=\"tp_nccL_stalls_emergency\"` This flips new requests to single GPU on the same nodes and should bypass NCCL. It's not ideal for throughput, but safe.

deploy-bot: route change applied to prod: rwd-llama-13b-quant -> single-gpu (gradual roll 10% -> 100%).

meera: after route flip, NCCL timeouts stop on the affected nodes. 5xx rate returning to baseline in ~10m. Latency for the model increased for some customers but availability is restored.

alex: good. We'll keep continuous batching disabled and the routing override in place. eng-runtime to implement consistent-hash partition hotfix and handshake for compatibility. ops to plan a controlled rolling restart for nodes that were stuck (after drain).

jamal: I'll open a branch with the partition change and a minimal handshake flag. Patch id: gitlab.com/redwood/runtime/commit/ea5f3b7 (emergency). Testing locally shows even shard sizes on the problematic tensor split.

eng-ml: schedule: hotfix review in 30m, can land and stage to 10% of prod nodes within 2 hours if approval goes smoothly. We should coordinate with customer_success for status updates.

customer_success: updated customers: short note sent, they appreciate rapid mitigation. Asking for postmortem and timeline for permanent fix.

ops_lead: Handoff: alex and meera will monitor for 1 hour to ensure stability. jamal and eng-ml will run the hotfix rollout plan and loop back here when 10% stage is live. Then we will schedule a postmortem runbook item: tag incident-1812345678 in PM board.

alex: monitoring looks clean. Keeping thread open for handoff. If anything spikes, page @ops_lead immediately.

oncall-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> degraded -> stabilized. Next steps: postmortem, alert tuning for batch_max_tokens auto-scaling, add regression test for TP partitioning with uneven tensor sizes.

ops_lead: assigning action items: ["eng-runtime: implement and test consistent-hash partition + handshake", "runtime: add canary for continuous-batching config spikes", "sre: add alert for per-shard partial_cache_entries > 500k", "prod-comm: customer CS follow-ups and incident summary"]. Will schedule postmortem doc and invite owners.

alex: thanks everyone. Closing realtime mitigation. Will update on postmortem doc with timeline and root cause once hotfix lands. :thumbsup:
